Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called? It’s been a few hours now and I just can’t get them to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure—let’s get that sorted. To start, could you please provide the phone number of the line that’s having trouble sending MMS?
Yes, of course. The phone number I’m using is 555-123-2002.
Please start by toggling Airplane Mode on and then off on your phone. This will reset all wireless radios. Once you’ve done that, let me know and we’ll move on to the next step.

No worries—it won’t affect any of your data. It’s just telling your phone to look for faster network options. 

Next, please set your network mode preference to “4G/5G Preferred.” On most phones you can do this by going to Settings → Connections (or Network) → Mobile Networks → Network Mode, then selecting “4G/5G Preferred.”  

Let me know when that’s done.

toolCalls.name: set_network_mode_preference
toolCalls.result:
Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

messages.content: Okay, I’ve set the network mode to “4G/5G Preferred” like you said. But I still see something about no signal and data being disabled at the top of my screen. Is that normal? What should I do now?

Next, please turn OFF Wi-Fi Calling on your phone. You can usually find this under Settings → Connections (or Network) → Wi-Fi Calling. 

Once you’ve toggled Wi-Fi Calling off, let me know and we’ll move on to the next step.

toolCalls.name: toggle_wifi_calling

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.

Understood. Let’s reset your APN settings next—this will correct any misconfigured MMS server URLs:

1. Open Settings → Connections (or Network) → Mobile Networks → Access Point Names.  
2. Tap the menu (⋮) and choose “Reset to default.”

Go ahead and reset the APN, then let me know when it’s done.

Rebooting won’t erase any of your photos or messages—it simply restarts your phone’s system. Please go ahead and reboot your device now (you can usually hold down the power button and select “Restart”). Once it’s back on, let me know and we’ll continue.

Next, let’s make sure your messaging app has the right permissions:

1. Open Settings → Apps (or Applications) → Messaging.  
2. Tap Permissions.  
3. Find “SMS” and set it to Allow.  

Please grant the SMS permission, then let me know and we’ll grant the storage permission next.

Some phones call the SMS app something else—like “Messages”, “Samsung Messages”, or “Google Messages.” Let’s try this:

1. Open Settings → Apps (or Applications).  
2. Scroll the list and look for the app you use to send texts—commonly named “Messages” or similar.  
3. Tap that app, then tap Permissions.  
4. Find “SMS” (or “Messaging”) and set it to Allow.

1. Power off your phone.
